title: Add auto-configuration for OTLP span exporter

timeline.body:
With these changes an OTLP HTTP/protobuf exporter is auto-configured if `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp` is on the classpath.

Closes gh-34390
Hey. We usually don't use the `enabled` properties to switch on/off features if there is another signal. In your case, the `OtlpHttpSpanExporter` on the classpath could be that feature.

reply.body: Both `OtlpHttpSpanExporter` and `OtlpGrpcSpanExporter` come from the same artifact (`io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-exporter-otlp`).

Ah, i didn't notice that, thanks. Then we have two options:

* leave the `enabled` property
* Remove the default from `endpoint` and use this as a trigger

I wonder if a third option would be to use a single property that takes an enum:

```
management.otlp.tracing.something=http
management.otlp.tracing.something=grpc
```
This would limit users to choose between http and grpc. Don't know if both are a valid use case, though.

No, I don't either. If it's valid, it could be a `Set<NewEnum>`:

```
management.otlp.tracing.something=grpc,http
```

If it isn't valid, a `NewEnum` property would be preferable as, unlike multiple `.enabled` properties, it prevents you from configuring something that's invalid.

FWIW, OpenTelemetry's own [autoconfigure module](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java/blob/main/sdk-extensions/autoconfigure/README.md#otlp-exporter-span-metric-and-log-exporters) exposes `otel.exporter.otlp.protocol` property with options `grpc` and `http/protobuf` which suggests the choice is usually exclusive. So IMO it makes sense to take the same approach in Spring Boot, and consider multiple exporters scenario as something that requires manual configuration.

I like the enum set idea, it makes the choice more clear/explicit.

I'm not sure why OTel does this, the SDK supports multiple exporters, right now Boot supports it as well (we also have auto-configuration for zipkin), I think we should able to follow this patterns instead what OTel does (we are also doing this in case of Micrometer registries).

I'm genuinely curious - how frequent is the multiple exporter scenario really?

Seems to me that offering a property that accepts a set of protocols makes it really easy to misconfigure things in a way that you end up sending the traces twice to the same collector, which you likely won't notice easily as the collector will deal with the duplicates.

I'm not sure about OTel, in Micrometer (slightly different scenario though) we see people using multiple registries.

To me, using the set of protocols makes this simpler and harder to misconfigure (than enabled flags) since it's explicit what transfer(s) are selected.

But I think I see your point and if I strictly apply this to Micrometer, there we only have one transport for the OTLP registry. And also, since the OTel SDK does not support every transports (HTTP/JSON is in spec. but not supported by the SDK), the Collectors need to support all 3 options. This drives me towards providing one option for OTLP and if people needs a different one for some reason, or two, they are just a `@Bean` away.
fyi: I updated the PR to provide one OTLP exporter.

> using the set of protocols makes this simpler and harder to misconfigure (than enabled flags)

Just to avoid confusion, I wasn't advocating for the enabled flags proposal, but for enum based solution originally proposed by Andy in https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/pull/34508#discussion_r1129226532 - so a property that takes a single protocol value, which results in an appropriate exporter being registered. I still see it as a good thing to align with what OTel does themselves.

In case someone wants multiple exporters, they can manually declare exporter beans causing the auto-configuration to back off. If find that approach quite analogous to what auto-configuration does in some other places.

Hi @jonatan-ivanov , I see that spring is diverging from the configuration properties proposed by the otel-sdk. For instance, the properties managed by this class maps to otel-sdk "otel.exporter.otlp.endpoint", "otel.exporter.otlp.compression" and so on...

Are there any plans to converge the config property names to the same used by otel-sdk ?

If no, isnt there another way to make them at least seem easier to map. E.g, spring version would only add the management.otlp prefix ?

reply.body:
Here's the rationale behind the current structure: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/30381 This PR follows that pattern.

There are at least two tricky things here:
1. There are at least two components that can export OTLP right now in Boot, the Micrometer Tracing OTel bridge (in this PR) and Micrometer's OTLP Meter Registry. I think users need to be able to configure them separately and `otel.exporter.otlp.endpoint` does not really make that distinction.
1. Under the hood, shipping OTLP does not need to use the OTel SDK at all, e.g.: Micrometer's OTLP registry does not use it, if for example Brave will add OTLP support, I guess that won't either. Check out the Zipkin properties and auto-configuration. Boot does not use OTel properties there and it needs to auto-configure either OTel or Brave based on those properties.

I think right now this is the easiest thing you can do to set these:
```
otel.exporter.otlp.xyz=...
management.otlp.metrics.export.xyz=${otel.exporter.otlp.xyz}
management.otlp.tracing.xyz=${otel.exporter.otlp.xyz} // maybe I should add export here?
```

I think we should figure out what would be the best and your feedback is apprechiated, right now this is what we have:
- [`OtlpProperties`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/spring-boot-project/spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/actuate/autoconfigure/metrics/export/otlp/OtlpProperties.java) for metrics
  - has a different prefix: `management.otlp.metrics.export` (this PR has `management.otlp.tracing`)
  - has a different property `url` (this PR calls it `endpoint`)
- [`ZipkinProperties`](https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/spring-boot-project/spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/actuate/autoconfigure/tracing/zipkin/ZipkinProperties.java) for tracing (Brave/OTel)
  - has similar prefix: `management.zipkin.tracing` (this PR follows that convention)
- [OTel SDK Properties](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java/blob/main/sdk-extensions/autoconfigure/README.md#exporters) 
  - has the prefix: `otel.exporter.otlp`
  - has similar properties

> 1. There are at least two components that can export OTLP right now in Boot, the Micrometer Tracing OTel bridge (in this PR) and Micrometer's OTLP Meter Registry. I think users need to be able to configure them separately and `otel.exporter.otlp.endpoint` does not really make that distinction.

Fair enough, makes sense as users could possibly use 2 different otel-compatible backends: one for metrics and other for tracing

> management.otlp.metrics.export.xyz=${otel.exporter.otlp.xyz}

Im doing the opposite: trying to support the SDK props as they are more widely known, so end-users would be able to configure it based on SDK docs, but it is really hard to map all the spring props to the sdk props. If it was just a matter of prefixes, life would be easier. But I understand the complexity and the other scenarios that you mention. There's even a more complex one such as `management.tracing.sampling.probability=${otel.traces.sampler.arg}` - the `otel.traces.sampler.arg` (urgh!) is a beast on its own as it includes inner properties on it depending on the sampler implementation. Perhaps somewhere in the docs we could have a section mapping the spring->otel-sdk properties.

> * has a different prefix: `management.otlp.metrics.export` (this PR has `management.otlp.tracing`)
> 
> * has a different property `url` (this PR calls it `endpoint`)

I personally like `management.otlp.tracing.export.http.endpoint` more. 
I also liked that you exposed all the OtlpHttpSpanExporterBuilder configurations, different from the `OpenTelemetryAutoConfiguration.otelSpanProcessor` which is using the BatchSpanProcessor internally and not offering the possibility to configure its propertyes such as batch/queue size, timeouts and so on...

reply.body:
I would still very much prefer the arrangement you @wilkinsona suggested in https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/pull/34508#discussion_r1129226532.

It feels like single exporter use case is the dominant one, and it's not like one exporter option is much more popular than the other one - AFAIK gRPC is still the default with OTel agent. So while I agree that HTTP exporter is the better default going forward, IMO auto-configuration should also provide value for those that prefer (or have to use) gRPC.

I missed the fact that `io.opentelemetry/opentelemetry-exporter-otlp` doesn't pull in gRPC dependencies (other dependency in my current project was pulling them in so just I wrongly assumed) and that of course changes things a bit and goes more in favor of providing auto-configuration for only HTTP exporter.

timeline.body: I'm not sure about this `Http` grouping, particularly if it turns out that the `enabled` property isn't needed. The main reason I'm not sure about it is that it's not consistent with what we've done for Zipkin where we have `management.tracing.zipkin.connect-timeout`, `management.tracing.zipkin.endpoint`, `management.tracing.zipkin.read-timeout`.

reply.body: Both `io.opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.http.trace.OtlpHttpSpanExporterBuilder` and `io.opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.trace.OtlpGrpcSpanExporterBuilder` have basically the same properties, so that also goes in favor of not having the grouping and reusing the same configuration properties for both HTTP and gRPC if the enum approach ends up being preferred.

With these changes an OTLP HTTP/protobuf exporter is auto-configured
if opentelemetry-exporter-otlp is on the classpath.

See gh-34508

timeline.body:
Hi @jonatan-ivanov , we are facing some issues integrating this into our project. The scenario is the following:

- we have a custom class that implements `SpanExporter` interface and internally wraps our own mutable `OtlpHttpSpanExporter`
- with this, we need to prevent the `OtlpAutoConfiguration` from creating the `OtlpHttpSpanExporter` Bean. However, the @ConditionalOnMissingBean is based only on OtlpHttpSpanExporter and OtlpGrpcSpanExporter beans, which is not our case as we implement `SpanExporter` interface and cannnot descend from the `OtlpHttpSpanExporter `since its final

Some possible solutions to my problem that I tried:
- Remove `OtlpAutoConfiguration`: this behavior is added by a internal library, so I cannot easily remove the `OtlpAutoConfiguration` without impacting the applications that uses our lib
- Replace the `SpanProcessor`: as the `OpenTelemetryAutoConfiguration.otelSpanProcessor` method does not have a `@ConditionalOnMissingBean`. I cannot easily replace the `SpanProcessor` with a custom one that would ignore the `OtlpHttpSpanExporter` Bean provided by `OtlpAutoConfiguration`
- Replace the `OpenTelemetryAutoConfiguration.otelSdkTracerProvider`: this would not work because the `SpanProcessor.otelSpanProcessor` will always instantiate a BatchSpanProcessor and start its thread. I'd have to shutdown it

Do you have any other suggestion on how can I overcome this ?

I was wondering if isn't the current `OtlpAutoConfiguration.otlpHttpSpanExporter` factory method too intrusive as it always provide a `SpanExporter` Bean even when the application has already defined its own `SpanExporter` ? Can we change this to a simple `@ConditionalOnMissingBean(SpanExporter.class)` ?
@chicobento I created a separate issue to discuss this, could you please check my answer there and reply to my questions? https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/issues/35596
